newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: GIO says can't explain share price rise.
newsitem.headline: GIO says can't explain share price rise.

text.p: Insurance group GIO Australia Holdings Ltd said on Thursday it could offer no explanation to the Australian Stock Exchange (ASX) about why its shares have risen so sharply in the last nine days.
GIO was responding to an ASX query about the 12 percent rise in the company's shares to a high of A$4.00 on April 23 from A$3.57 on April 14.
"We can offer no explanation for the price change in the comapny's shares," the company said in a statement.
On Tuesday, the Sydney Morning Herald newspaper reported that there was a rumour that Australia's largest bank, National Australia Bank Ltd, was examining the possibility of acquiring GIO.
The paper also said there was some speculation that GIO had become more vulnerable as a takeover target since the release of the Wallis Inquiry into Australia's financial system earlier this month.

The shares of GIO competitor, QBE Insurance Ltd, have also risen sharply in the past week. Dealers said funds had flown towards the insurance sector recently after the spotlight being on the bank sector in the lead up and following the release of the Wallis report.
On Friday, Melbourne-based fund manager Portfolio Partners Ltd revealed that it had lifted its interest in GIO to 7.6 percent from 6.5 percent.
At 10.15 a.m (0015 GMT), GIO shares were one cent weaker at A$3.85 on light turnover.
